name.text: DJR Q01 - What is R?

questiontext.text: What is R?

answer.text: A programming language and environment for data analysis
A folder used to store CSV files

name.text: DJR Q02 - R and RStudio

questiontext.text: What is the relationship between R and RStudio?

answer.text: RStudio is the programming language, while R runs the code
R is the programming language, while RStudio provides an interface for working with R
R and RStudio are two names for the same software

name.text: DJR Q03 - R Projects and relative paths

questiontext.text: Working inside an R Project makes it easier to use relative paths and share an analysis with other people.

name.text: DJR Q04 - Installing and loading packages

questiontext.text: Which statement correctly describes installing and loading a package?

answer.text: Run install.packages() every time you open RStudio
Install the package once, then load it with library() in each new R session
A package remains loaded after RStudio is closed

name.text: DJR Q05 - What is the tidyverse?

answer.text: A replacement for the R programming language
A collection of R packages that follow related design principles

name.text: DJR Q06 - Packages across R sessions

questiontext.text: After running library(tidyverse) once, tidyverse will remain loaded even after you close and reopen RStudio.

The path does not include the package name

name.text: DJR Q46 - Ranking grouped totals

questiontext.text: A public-spending dataset contains many payments made by each department. Which code ranks departments by their total spending?

answer.text:
spending |>
  group_by(department) |>
  summarise(total = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(total))

spending |>
  arrange(desc(amount)) |>
  group_by(department) |>
  summarise(total = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE))

spending |>
  group_by(department) |>
  summarise(total = mean(amount, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(total))

name.text: DJR Q47 - Grouping after summarising

questiontext.text:
A student writes the following code. Why does it not calculate the number of complaints in each district?

complaints |>
  summarise(total = n()) |>
  group_by(district)

answer.text: group_by() can only be used with numeric columns
The data were summarised before being grouped, so the district information is no longer available

name.text: DJR Q48 - Complete grouped analysis pipeline

questiontext.text: A transport dataset contains district, route, and delay_minutes. A journalist wants to find the routes in Kowloon with the highest average delay. Which workflow is correct?

answer.text:
delays |>
  filter(district == "Kowloon") |>
  group_by(route) |>
  summarise(average_delay = mean(delay_minutes, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(average_delay))

The hospital has the largest number of recorded visits, which may include repeat visits
The hospital had the longest waiting time
